subject.title: feat(onboarding): offer detected Claude Code/Codex/Hermes memory imports across CLI, macOS, and Linux onboarding

question: Should this broad onboarding rollout wait for the migration backup hang to be fixed, or should the PR be narrowed to surfaces that can prove bounded completion?
rationale: The branch intentionally exposes a pre-existing migration operation to first-time users, and its own live proof shows that operation can hang indefinitely; deciding whether to block the rollout or narrow its scope requires ownership of the migration and onboarding release boundary.

options.title: Fix before rollout
options.body: Resolve or bound the backup traversal, add cancellation or visible recovery, and prove all onboarding surfaces complete successfully before merge.

options.title: Narrow the PR
options.body: Land only the shared migration and already-proven CLI work, deferring Linux, Control UI, and native macOS onboarding entry points until their complete flows are proven.

options.title: Accept the known hang
options.body: Ship all entry points with the known possibility that a first-run import remains indefinitely blocked, explicitly owning the onboarding availability risk.

recommendation.title: Fix before rollout
recommendation.body: Resolve or bound the backup traversal, add cancellation or visible recovery, and prove all onboarding surfaces complete successfully before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest available adjacent setup/Codex history and authored the cross-surface design being evaluated.
